explanation:
The exit function in C is used to terminate the calling process immediately with a specified status code. It is employed to end a program abruptly, signal success or failure, or handle errors. Modern implementations do not close open streams or file descriptors, as the operating system kernel automatically handles this upon process termination, avoiding unnecessary overhead and improving efficiency.

The exit() function in C is a standard library function that immediately terminates the calling process. It is used to end program execution gracefully or with an error indication, allowing the program to return a status code to the operating system, which helps in debugging and script automation by signaling success (0) or failure (non-zero).
